01-welcome.png.t: Connect Azure — opens the Add a cloud window on the Azure tab. It only asks for a connection string; nothing is read until you press Connect there.
Add a cloud — the same window, from anywhere in the app. Use it later to connect AWS or Google Cloud as well.
Simple | Advanced — Simple is where you act. Advanced is read-only pages (ledger, signatures, agents); it never changes anything.
Help — opens the Help panel with task-shaped answers and the keyboard shortcuts.
Connect AWS / Connect Google — the same Add a cloud window, on the AWS or Google Cloud tab. You do not need them for Azure.

02-add-cloud.png.t: Cloud tabs — Azure Service Bus is selected. The AWS and Google tabs ask for different credentials.
Where do I get the connection string? — expands the portal steps, with the permissions to give.
Name — what you will see in ServiceHub. It is a label only; it does not change anything in Azure.
Environment — Development, UAT or Production. Start with Development; Auto Replay never acts in Production.
Connection string — paste the Primary connection string of a Shared access policy (Manage, Send, Listen). It is encrypted on this server and never shown again.
Show value — reveals what you typed so you can check it. It cannot reveal a stored string.
Cancel — closes the window; nothing is saved.
Connect — tests the string, then saves it. It only reads queues; it never sends or deletes anything by itself.
(?) — opens Help on this very screen. Every window has one.
✕ — closes the window without saving (Esc does the same).

02-add-cloud-help.png.t: Settings → Shared access policies — in the Azure portal, on your Service Bus namespace.
Tick Manage, Send and Listen. Azure only lets Manage list your queues and count messages; Send is used only when you replay.
Copy the Primary connection string — it starts with Endpoint=sb://.
The form underneath — the cloud tabs, Name, Environment, Connection string and Show value, exactly as in the previous screenshot.

03-add-cloud-filled.png.t: The connection string, hidden as you paste it.
Connect — tests the connection, then saves it.
The rest of the form — cloud tabs, Environment, Show value and Cancel, as described on the previous screenshot.

04-connected.png.t: The result: how many queues, topics and subscriptions ServiceHub found, how many messages are dead-lettered, and whether this cloud can prove a replay held.
Open Home — closes the window and shows Home.

05-home.png.t: Window — the period Home counts over (24 hours, 7 or 30 days). It changes what you see, never what happens.
The Agent bar — what the Agent is doing, how many replays it verified, and how many it is still watching.
Pause — stops the Agent acting until someone resumes it. It keeps watching and recording. Your own replays still work.
What this cloud can do — ticks show what Azure lets ServiceHub do safely (count, watch, browse, prove a fix held, scheduled messages).
Dead letters — opens the list of messages that failed and were set aside.
Active messages — browse what is waiting. On Azure, looking is not a delivery.
Replayed — everything put back, by whom, and how it went.
Auto Replay rules — opens the rules panel. A rule only acts once a failure has earned it.
Got it — hides this explanation. It does not affect your data.
See all dead letters in Azure — opens the Dead letters list for this cloud.
Help for this page (the book beside the title) — opens Help on this very page, over it. Every page has one.

05b-navigation.png.t: Back — returns to the previous place in the app.
Forward — goes to the place you came back from.
Search (⌘K) — jump to a cloud, queue or page. Searching never changes anything.
The bell — the only place the Agent asks you something. A number appears when it needs you.
Simple — the two pages where you do the work.
You — who ServiceHub records actions as, with your role.
Dead letters — messages that failed, with the reason and a Replay button.
Active messages — what is waiting now.
Replayed — what was put back and whether it stayed fixed.
Auto Replay — rules for retries ServiceHub may do on its own.
Your cloud — pick it to see only that cloud. The dot shows the connection is healthy.
Connections — your connected clouds, to test or remove.
Add a cloud — connect another cloud.
Settings — connections, notifications, preferences, access and backup.
Home — the overview: what needs attention, what the Agent is doing, and how replays ended.

06-dead-letters.png.t: Namespace picker — all of Azure, or one namespace.
Why they failed — the biggest reasons, counted. The reason comes from what your sender wrote when it dead-lettered the message.
Dead letters tab — messages set aside. The number is how many are stuck now.
Active tab — what is waiting in the queue.
Replayed tab — what has been put back.
Reason chips — click one to show only that reason.
Help for this page — opens Help on this page’s step of the guide. The (?) beside it only re-shows the short explanation.

07-filters-and-table.png.t: Showing — Stuck now, or messages that have since left the queue.
Time window — only messages set aside in this period.
Search — by message ID, queue, reason or error text.
Replay All Messages — opens a preview of everything shown. Nothing is sent until you confirm the preview.
Refresh — reads the queue again. On Azure this is free. The ⓘ beside it says when it was last read.
Selection — tick rows to act on several; this line shows how many.
Replay selected — opens the same preview for just the ticked messages.
Details — opens the message: why it failed, its body, properties and delivery history.
Replay — opens the proposal for this one message. It does not send anything yet.

The table — a tick on every row (the one in the heading ticks the whole page), Details and Replay on every row, and an ⓘ About button on each column heading that explains that column in a sentence. “View details” in the heading chooses which columns show.
Reason chips — each shows a reason and how many messages have it. Click one to show only those; click it again to show all.
All queues & topics — limit the list to one queue or topic.
The selection bar — the tick selects every row on this page; View details chooses which columns show; Replay selected stays dimmed until something is ticked.

08-message-details.png.t: Expand — widens the panel for long messages.
Overview — reason, why it failed, the body with the bad field marked.
Delivery — the delivery history Azure recorded.
Why it failed — a plain-words reading of the recorded reason. Marked Suggestion: it is a reading, not something Azure reported.
Formatted / Raw — switch the body view.
Replay this message — opens the proposal. Nothing is sent from here.
Body, Properties and Headers — the other tabs; each is shown below.
Formatted and Copy body — pretty-print the body, or copy it to your clipboard. The copy stays in your browser.
Copy message ID — copies the ID so you can search for it elsewhere.

08-message-details-body.png.t: The message body exactly as it was sent.
Expand widens the panel; the other tabs (Overview, Body, Properties, Headers, Delivery) switch what is shown.
Formatted / Raw switch the view; Copy body copies it to your clipboard.

08-message-details-properties.png.t: Application properties and system properties (message ID, content type, subject).
Expand widens the panel; the other tabs (Overview, Body, Properties, Headers, Delivery) switch what is shown.

08-message-details-headers.png.t: Broker headers: enqueued time, lock and sequence information.
Expand widens the panel; the other tabs (Overview, Body, Properties, Headers, Delivery) switch what is shown.

08-message-details-delivery.png.t: How many times Azure tried, and when it set the message aside.
Expand widens the panel; the other tabs (Overview, Body, Properties, Headers, Delivery) switch what is shown.

09-replay-proposal.png.t: The message — what is about to be replayed: ID, where it is stuck, when and why it was set aside, and its body.
Replay 1 message — sends it back. It is only sent when you press this.
What will happen, Safety checks, After it runs — fold open or closed; the next screenshot shows them open.

09-replay-proposal-checks.png.t: What will happen — where it goes and what happens to the dead-letter copy (it is removed once Azure accepts the new one).
Safety checks — every check that must pass; a failing one blocks the replay and says why.
After it runs — ServiceHub records it and watches for 24 hours; if it comes back, nothing retries it.
The folding headings and the Replay button repeated at the end of the window.

07b-selection.png.t: Row tick — choose which messages to act on. The header tick chooses every row on the page.
Selection count — how many messages are ticked.
Clear — unticks everything. Nothing else changes.
Replay selected — opens the bulk preview for just these messages. Nothing is sent yet.
The filter row — reason chips, Showing, Time window, queue, search, Replay All Messages and Refresh, each explained on the previous screenshot.
The table — the ticks, Details and Replay on every row, and the whole-page tick in the heading.
The selection bar — the whole-page tick and View details (which columns show).

13-bulk-replay.png.t: Preview — nothing has run yet. Step 1 of Preview → Run → Watch.
Held back — messages that fail a safety check stay in dead letters; they are never forced.
Grouped by how they failed — so you can see whether you are fixing one problem or several.
Where each one goes — the queue each message will be sent back to.
Replay N messages — sends them one at a time, re-checking each. You can stop partway.
Page controls — move through the list when more messages are chosen than fit on one page.
How it will run — folds open to show the pace and the automatic stop (five failures in a row).

10-replay-result.png.t: The result, in plain words: it was sent back, and ServiceHub will watch for it coming back.
It is recorded, with who did it, and shows under Replayed (and in Advanced → Recovery Ledger).
Active messages / Replayed — jump to where you can watch this message.

11-replayed.png.t: Messages replayed — how many were put back in the window.
Being watched — replays still inside their watch window. Azure can prove whether each stayed fixed.
Came back — messages that failed the same way again. Nothing retries them on its own.
Result filter — stayed fixed, being watched, came back.
Download — saves this list as a file. It does not change anything.
Details — the full record of this replay.
Filters — namespace, queue or topic, result, time window and search; Refresh reads the list again. They change what is listed, never what happened.
The table — a tick per replay (the heading tick ticks the page) and Details on each row.
What am I looking at? — a short reading guide. Auto Replay rules — opens the rules page. All and Last 24 hours — the result and time filters.
The three tabs — Dead letters, Active and Replayed. They switch the list below without leaving the page.

12-active.png.t: Send a message — puts a test message on the queue. This does change the queue, so use a dev queue.
Counts — waiting, oldest, delivered before, dead-lettered.
Filters — queue or topic, message state, time window and search.
Follow live — shows new messages as they arrive. On Azure, looking does not count as a delivery.
Auto-refresh — re-reads the queue every 15 seconds.
Scheduled — messages set to arrive later.
Peek message — opens one message to read it. Peeking does not remove or lock it.
Filters and tools — namespace, queue, time window, search, how often the list refreshes, Refresh now, and Download body (saves the shown messages’ bodies as a file; changes nothing).
Dead-lettered — jumps to the dead letters in this queue.
The table — a tick per message (the heading tick ticks the page) and Details on each row.
What am I looking at? — a short reading guide. The queue and time-window pickers narrow what is listed.
The three tabs — Dead letters, Active and Replayed. They switch the list below without leaving the page.

14-auto-replay.png.t: Auto Generate Rules — proposes rules from failures already seen. It only proposes; you decide what to turn on.
Create rule — start a rule from a failure you have already seen.
How it works — you name a failure, safety checks decide, it replays gently, it proves it worked and stops itself if it does not.
Totals — rules on, replayed by rules, waiting for a person, stopped themselves.
Namespace — Auto Replay rules apply to every Azure namespace; this picks which one the page shows.
Refresh rules — reads the rules again.
Create your first rule — the same as Create rule, shown while there are none.

14-auto-replay-create.png.t: Based on — pick a failure ServiceHub has already seen. A rule can only be made from a seen failure.
The guarantees: never in Production, same safety checks as you, and it stops itself if fewer than half stay fixed.
Create and turn on — enabled once you choose a failure.
The page header — namespace, Refresh rules, Auto Generate Rules (proposes only) and the “How Auto Replay works” fold, as on the previous screenshot.

15-settings-connections.png.t: Sections — Connections, Notifications, Preferences, Access & security and Backup. Each jumps to that part of this window.
Add a cloud — connect another cloud.
Test — checks the connection now and shows the result. Reads only.
Remove — forgets this connection and its stored credential. It does not delete anything in Azure.

15-settings-notifications.png.t: In-app bell and pop-up — always on. It cannot be switched off, so it can never be switched off by mistake.
Add webhook (Slack) — paste a Slack incoming-webhook URL to also get the message there.
Add webhook (Microsoft Teams) — the same for a Teams channel.
Add webhook (any other system) — JSON to a URL you choose. Private and internal addresses are refused.

15-settings-preferences.png.t: Theme — Light today; Dark is marked soon.
Times shown in — your browser’s time zone, or UTC. It changes how times are displayed, never the data.
Open on — start in Simple every time (Simple), or where you last were (Last used). Kept in this browser only.

15-settings-access.png.t: Who you are — shown from this browser session until roles are switched on. The credential key fingerprint shows what encrypts stored credentials.
Roles — Viewer sees, Operator replays, Approver answers the Agent, Admin connects clouds. Giving the first role switches roles on.
Who — the API key name or signed-in user the role is for.
Kind, Role, Where and Grant — choose whether it is a key or a person, the role, whether it applies everywhere or to one namespace, then Grant. Granting the first role switches roles on for everyone.
Emergency stop — type STOP, say why, and switch it on to halt every automatic action at once. Nothing already done is undone; switch it off to resume.

15-settings-backup.png.t: Take a backup now — saves a consistent copy of ServiceHub’s own database (not of your clouds).

16-help.png.t: Search — type what you are trying to do.
An answer — click to open it in place; each links to the screen it is about.
Setting up answers — connecting, alerts and who may replay.
Keyboard shortcuts — only ones that work are listed.

Step by step — one guide per cloud, each with every screen as a real screenshot and a numbered key for every button and link. Yours (Azure) is listed first. The same guides are the articles in docs/clouds.

17-advanced-overview.png.t: Window — the period the page counts over.
Insights — patterns ServiceHub noticed across your failures.
Recovery — how replays ended. “Recovered” means it did not come back, not that the business transaction completed.
Authority — what each failure may do on its own, and what holds it there.
Capability — what each cloud can prove.
Being watched, All agents → and Recovery Ledger → — jump to the Agents page and the Recovery Ledger. They only open pages; nothing changes.
Overview — the page you are on; the other three Advanced pages are in the bar at the top.

18-search.png.t: Search box — type part of a cloud, queue or page name. Enter opens the first result. Esc closes. Searching never changes anything.

18-bell.png.t: The bell — the only place the Agent asks you something. It lists what is waiting for you and clears when it is resolved, not when you look.
See all waiting — opens the full list of what needs a person.

18-user-menu.png.t: Settings — opens Settings (connections, notifications, preferences, access, backup).
You — who ServiceHub records your actions as, and whether this server has sign-in turned on.

17-advanced-ledger.png.t: Export evidence — downloads the ledger so it can be verified offline. It changes nothing.
Outcome chips — Waiting, Watching, Recovered, Unverified, Returned, Failed, Unknown, Declined. Recovered and Unverified are never counted together.
Filters — cloud, namespace, queue or topic, who did it, and search.
Details — who took the action, what happened and its evidence. Each entry carries a fingerprint of the one before it.
Filters and entries — namespace, queue or topic, who, and search narrow the list; each entry opens to show its evidence.
What am I looking at? — a short reading guide for this page. Window — the period it counts over.
Outcome chips with counts — click one to list only those entries; All shows everything again.
Paging — how many rows per page, previous, the page number and next.
About buttons (ⓘ) on the column headings — each explains that column in a sentence. They change nothing.

17-advanced-signatures.png.t: Trace a message — follow one message across clouds by its ID.
Growing — signatures whose recent days hold at least twice what earlier days did.
A signature — one way of failing: the same queue and the same kind of error, so many messages become one thing to reason about.
Replays — how many of these were replayed and how many were verified to have held.
Filters — cloud, namespace, queue or topic, who, and search.
Each signature row — opens to show the failures grouped under it and what each replay did.
What am I looking at? — a short reading guide. Window — the period counted.
Chips — Signatures, All, Replay helps, Replay doesn’t help. Click one to list only those.
Paging — rows per page, previous, the page number and next.
About buttons (ⓘ) on the column headings — each explains that column in a sentence. They change nothing.

17-advanced-agents.png.t: Acting agents — the only ones that can change anything, and only after the same safety checks you get.
Watching agents — they only look and record.
Pause — stops that agent acting. It is the one thing Advanced can do, because it only removes authority. Nothing it already did is undone.
Learn more — a short explanation of how agents work.
Health summary, agent rows and Open — the summary says whether every agent is running normally; a row opens that agent’s details; Open goes to the screen the agent works through.
What am I looking at? — a short reading guide for this page.

05c-home-middle.png.t: Why messages failed — the reasons among the dead letters, biggest first, with how many each has. The window buttons (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days) set the period; Show as table swaps the chart for a table.
How replays ended — what happened to the replays in this window.
7, 14, 30 days and Show as table — change the period Home counts over, or show the numbers as a table. They never change what happens.
Latest dead letters and Recent activity — shown in full on the next screenshot.
Window buttons (7, 14, 30 days) and Open → — change the period, or open that item’s page. They never change what happens.

05d-home-end.png.t: The latest dead letters, each with Details → — the same message view as on the Dead letters tab. “See all →” opens the full list.
Recent activity — what ServiceHub and people did, newest first. Each line opens to show its detail; nothing here changes anything.
Open → — opens that item’s page. It only navigates.
Connected — a note that a namespace was connected, with when and by whom. Opens to show the detail.
Window buttons, Show as table, and the reasons — each reason opens the dead letters with that reason. They only change what is shown.

07c-table-end.png.t: The foot of the table — the same ticks, Details and Replay on every row.
Paging — rows per page, previous, the page numbers and next.

13b-bulk-replay-end.png.t: How it will run — the pace (a few messages a second, gentle on your consumer) and the automatic stop: five failures in a row.
After they are sent back — what ServiceHub does next: it records each replay and watches for 24 hours.
No purge on Azure — this cloud cannot delete one message on its own, so ServiceHub does not offer “Purge instead…” here (AWS and Google Cloud do).
Replay N messages — sends them one at a time, re-checking each. You can stop partway.
Page controls — move through the list when more messages are chosen than fit on one page.

11b-replayed-end.png.t: The replays, newest first — each with a tick and Details.
Paging — rows per page, previous, the page numbers and next.
The three tabs, the Auto Replay rules button, and the table headings with their ⓘ About buttons — as on the previous screenshot.
Filters — result, queue or topic, time window and search; Refresh re-reads the list and Download as CSV saves it as a file. They change what is listed, never what happened.

12b-active-end.png.t: A message row — a tick to choose it, and Details to open it (body, properties, delivery). Looking at an Azure message is not a delivery.
Paging — rows per page, previous, the page numbers and next.
The controls above the table — the same filters, search, auto-refresh, Refresh, Scheduled, and the ⓘ About buttons on the column headings, as on the previous screenshot.

16b-help-end.png.t: Step by step — one guide per cloud, each with every screen as a real screenshot and a numbered key for every button and link.
Answers — click one to open it in place; each links to the screen it is about.

17b-advanced-agents-more.png.t: Watching agents — they only look and record; they cannot change anything.
Each agent row opens to show what it may and may not do; Open goes to the screen it works through; Pause (acting agents only) stops it acting.

17a-advanced-agents-middle.png.t: Agent rows — click a row to see what that agent may and may not do; Open goes to the screen it works through; Pause (acting agents only) stops it acting.
More agent rows — the acting agents (Bulk Replay, Auto Replay) and the rest; each opens to show what it may do.

17c-advanced-agents-rows.png.t: Agent rows — click a row to see what that agent may and may not do; Open goes to the screen it works through; Pause (acting agents only) stops it acting.
